text:
maggie: Heads up — after flipping the fncall strict-validate canary to 20% we saw a big uptick in rejects. Trying to decide if we should back it out or pivot to a 'soft-validate' handshake instead.

devon: how big is the uptick? any sample payloads?

maggie: spike at 03:14 UTC, fncall_schema_reject_rate jumped ~6x. small sample log: ```WARN validate(fncall): account=12345 req_id=rc_7a1 shape_mismatch: missing required field 'args.items[0].price'```

leo: right now strict-validate = immediate hard reject and we short-circuit the tool invocation. That keeps downstream from seeing bad payloads but causes noisy fails and hard reject telemetry.

jay: downstream billing note — if we forward bad payloads to the tool we'll charge tokens. We need to decide billing semantics for soft accepts. Can't surprise customers.

pm-ellie: UX idea: soft-validate mode = accept request, call tool, return a response but mark it with validation.status = "soft_reject" and show it on Console. Then offer a quick UI action: "Add sample to schema allowlist" or "Request fix". That gives operators a workflow.

devon: implementation thought: runtime adds header `X-Redwood-Validation-Mode: soft` for canary accounts. Validator returns metadata {validation: "soft", score: 0.72}. Runtime writes metric `fncall.soft_validate_count` and tags route/model/account. We also sample 1% full payloads to S3 for triage.

leo: two risks: 1) routing — if we accept then route to regular model variant the app sees the same output as before and won't trigger fallback. We probably want policy: on soft_validate -> still allow fallback to degen route if the result quality is below threshold. 2) latency — extra telemetry + sampling might add ms.

maggie: agreed. Proposed routing policy: soft_validate = pass-through to primary tool, attach validation metadata in response; if subsequent post-process detects output shape mismatch OR validator score < threshold -> route to fallback variant and surface an incident in console. 

jay: re: billing: if we decide soft_validate leads to tool execution, we must bill for tool tokens. Alternative: do a cheap preflight validation pass (no model run) and if it fails convert to early-decline but still show soft flag. That avoids extra charges but reduces fidelity. Which do we want?

devon: preflight-only preserves cost but misses cases where model behavior interacts with malformed tool input. Some real bugs only appear once the tool executes. I think default soft_validate should execute tool; billing warning in console + an opt-out per-account.

pm-ellie: Console additions: new panel "Fncall validation" with columns: sample payload, validation status (soft/hard), account, route, action buttons (promote, ignore, request-fix). Also surface SLA impacts and estimated extra token cost.

console-team: UI note — we need to show aggregated counts and a timeline so PMs can see if a schema change caused the spike. Also toggles to filter by canary flag.

leo: telemetry detail: add gauges `fncall.soft_sampled_payload_count`, `fncall.soft_to_hard_escalations`. Export tags: model, route, validator_version, canary_flag. For privacy, payloads stored encrypted and accessible only to SE/owner.

maggie: operational rollout: start with an internal-only canary (seed accounts + console team) -> 1% of external traffic -> widen. Provide SDK header `X-Redwood-Validation-OptIn: true` for partners who want it.

devon: code snippet for validator handshake (rough): ```http
POST /v1/invoke
Headers: X-Redwood-Validation-Mode: soft
Body: {"prompt":..., "fncall": {...}}
-- runtime -> validator -> runtime attaches metadata -> runtime calls tool -> response includes validation metadata
```

jay: liability check — legal wants a short copy for Console explaining "soft-validate may cause additional tool calls and charges; customers can opt out". Add to rollout checklist.

maggie: perf question — will sampling + metrics cause cardinality explosion in our TSDB? keep tagset minimal and sample across accounts. Also enforce sampling queue size and backpressure.

leo: agreed, limit tags to model, route, validation_result, validator_version. Use hashed account id for index to avoid cardinality.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary flag `fncall.soft_validate` enabled for internal seed group at 2026-03-18T03:23:10Z :rocket:

devon: next steps I can do: RFC describing the handshake, telemetry sketch, metrics names, console wireframe. Who owns the SDK header docs?

pm-ellie: I'll own docs + console copy. leo + devon own runtime changes. maggie will coordinate rollout and alerting thresholds. jay will follow up on billing language with finance.

maggie: ok. Quick question for the group — what should be the default sampling rate for full payload capture for initial rollout? I'm thinking 1% global, 5% for accounts in the canary.

leo: 1% global 5% canary sounds fine. Also record a small example payload inline in telemetry event for fast triage (no S3 fetch) but keep that to <200 bytes.

devon: I'll add config flags: `soft_validate.sample_rate`, `soft_validate.canary_rate`, `soft_validate.backpressure_limit`. Will include eviction policy.

pm-ellie: +1. I'll draft console mockups and a short help blurb.

maggie: cool — I'll open the RFC and link the canary list. If we see nontrivial soft->hard escalations we'll pause. Thanks all :thumbsup:
